blocks.text: 1. Text Normalization

blocks.alt: Raw text goes through normalization to produce consistent text

blocks.text: Data Cleaning covered removing noise from raw text. Text Normalization picks up from there, shifting focus from removing noise to standardizing form.
It makes equivalent text look identical before it reaches chunking.
2. Cleaning Versus Normalization

blocks.alt: Cleaning removes noise while normalization standardizes form

blocks.text: Data Cleaning and normalization are related but distinct. Cleaning removes noise; normalization standardizes what remains.
They are two distinct, sequential preparation steps.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Step","What it does"],"rows":[["Data cleaning","Removes boilerplate, encoding issues, corrupted text"],["Text normalization","Standardizes casing, Unicode form, punctuation, and formats"]]}

blocks.text: 3. Case Folding Consistency

blocks.alt: Hello and hello fold into the same token

blocks.text: The same word written in different cases looks like two different strings to a naive comparison.
Consistent casing helps later comparison and search steps treat them as the same.
4. Unicode Normalization

blocks.alt: An accented word normalizes into Unicode NFC form

blocks.text: The same visible character can be represented by different underlying Unicode sequences.
Normalizing to one consistent form avoids subtle, invisible mismatches later.

blocks.title: warn
blocks.content: Two strings that look identical on screen can fail an exact match comparison if their underlying Unicode sequences differ, a subtle bug that Unicode normalization directly prevents.

blocks.text: 5. Punctuation And Special Characters

blocks.alt: Smart quotes normalize into straight quotes

blocks.text: Smart quotes, stray symbols, and inconsistent punctuation vary across sources.
Standardizing them keeps downstream text processing predictable.
6. Number And Date Formats

blocks.alt: One date format is compared against another date format

blocks.text: Dates and numbers appear written in many different formats across sources.
Standardizing them makes later retrieval and comparison far more reliable.
7. When Normalization Goes Too Far
Over aggressive normalization can strip meaning a model actually needed.
Code snippets and proper nouns deserve lighter, more careful handling.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: Lowercasing an entire document can erase the distinction between a proper noun and a common word, or between a code identifier and ordinary text, so normalization rules need to be applied selectively.

blocks.text: 8. Normalization As The Consistency Layer
Every cleaned document, regardless of source, passes through this same standardization step.
This produces consistent text ready for metadata extraction, covered as a later topic in this module.
9. Recognizing When Text Normalization Needs Extra Care

blocks.alt: Multilingual or mixed formats point toward investing in normalization

blocks.text: Multi source, multi language pipelines benefit most from thorough normalization.
Code heavy technical documents need lighter, more careful normalization instead.
10. Worked Example
The example below demonstrates case folding and Unicode normalization.

code.content:
import unicodedata

documents = [
    "Machine Learning is POWERFUL.",
    "machine learning is powerful.",
    "Café",       # accented form
    "Cafe\u0301", # visually identical, different underlying sequence
]

def normalize_text(text):
    text = text.lower()
    text = unicodedata.normalize("NFC", text)
    return text

print("Before normalization:")
for doc in documents:
    print(f"  {doc!r}")

normalized = [normalize_text(doc) for doc in documents]
print("\nAfter normalization:")
for doc in normalized:
    print(f"  {doc!r}")

print(f"\nThe two 'machine learning' variants now match: {normalized[0] == normalized[1]}")
print(f"The two 'cafe' variants now match: {normalized[2] == normalized[3]}")

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: Running this example shows two sentences that differed only in casing becoming identical strings, and two visually identical accented words becoming identical Unicode sequences.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Confusing normalization with cleaning and skipping one of the two distinct steps.
Ignoring Unicode form differences that make visually identical text compare as unequal.
Lowercasing an entire document without preserving meaningful casing in code or proper nouns.
Leaving dates and numbers in inconsistent formats, hurting later retrieval and comparison.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: Text normalization standardizes cleaned text so equivalent content looks identical.
Cleaning removes noise; normalization standardizes what remains, two distinct steps.
Consistent casing helps later comparison and search treat equivalent words as the same.
The same visible character can have different underlying Unicode sequences without normalization.
Standardizing punctuation and special characters keeps downstream processing predictable.
Standardizing date and number formats makes retrieval and comparison far more reliable.
Over aggressive normalization can strip meaning from code snippets and proper nouns.
Normalization acts as a consistency layer before metadata extraction begins.
